newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania police boss quits after diplomat attacked.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania police boss quits after diplomat attacked.

text.p: The head of the police force in Lithuania's capital has resigned because of an attack on a French diplomat, the government said on Wednesday.
The diplomat, Patrick Donabedian, suffered a cerebral hemorrhage and had to undergo surgery after he was badly beaten and robbed by three youths near his home on Sunday evening.
The government press office said Vilnius chief commissioner of police Vytautas Leipus resigned "because he felt moral responsibility for this event which has damaged the state's image so much."
Donabedian is still being held in intensive care. Doctors say he cannot be moved to France for at least a week, Levret Didier, French embassy charge d'affaires, told Reuters.
Didier said foreign diplomats, increasingly worried by violent incidents, would meet on Wednesday and then take their concerns to Interior Minister Vidmantas Zhiemelis.
In March, a Japanese diplomat and his wife were beaten by a group of hooligans after a world cup soccer qualifying match.
The Interior Ministry said it had detained three suspects who confessed to being involved in the attack on Donabedian.
